title: Chicken, wing, meat and skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken wings are the portion of the bird that includes meat, skin, and bone. In their raw state they provide protein, fat, B‑vitamins, and minerals such as iron and zinc. Wings are widely used for frying, baking, or cooking in sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Wings are one of the most popular snack foods worldwide, especially in the United States (e.g., "Buffalo wings").
Chicken wings contain more fat than most other chicken cuts because of the skin.
In the US more than 1.5 billion servings of wings are consumed each year.
Wings are often served with butter‑based hot sauce mixtures.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Protein from chicken supports tissue growth, repair, and the synthesis of enzymes and hormones.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Niacin (B3) and pyridoxine (B6) help with energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Iron and zinc in wings are important for immune health and blood formation.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of protein and fat helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Raw chicken wings may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C (165 °F).

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The skin adds calories; people watching their weight may remove the skin or choose leaner cuts.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals can develop allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wings can be fried, baked, boiled, or grilled. Removing excess fat and skin before cooking reduces calories. Marinades with soy sauce, honey, garlic, or hot sauce add flavor. Serve with vegetable sides, dips, or as a finger food.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw wings in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C for up to 2 days. For longer storage freeze at ‑18 °C; they remain good for up to 9 months. Thaw in the fridge before cooking, not at room temperature.
